The tables are simple and documented in the header, but the multipliers were not checked against a reference here.

terms.meaning: The kind of quantity a unit measures, such as length, voltage or time.
The number that turns a value in one unit into the standard unit.
A number the 3D model is allowed to use for sizing or placing things.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Table of known units
sections.what: Lists recognised unit names with their standard unit, dimension and conversion factor, such as millimetres to metres and feet to metres. Names not in the table are unknown.
sections.why: Stated in the header: quantity dimensions are explicit, with no inferred units.
sections.watch_out: Short names such as a, d and h are read as amps, days and hours, so a mislabeled unit would be converted wrongly.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Which fact types use which dimension
sections.what: Maps fact types such as width, height, voltage, current, count, duration and angle to a dimension, so a value is only used when its unit matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops a value with the wrong kind of unit from being used as a quantity.
sections.watch_out: A fact type missing from this map is never used as a model quantity, only kept as evidence.

sections.name: semantic_key
sections.title: Normalizing names for comparison
sections.what: Makes text comparable by collapsing extra spaces and ignoring capital letters.
sections.why: Likely reason: so names that differ only in spacing or case match the same rule.
sections.watch_out: Only spacing and case are normalized; spelling differences still produce different keys.

sections.name: model_unit_eligible
sections.title: Whether a value can drive the model
sections.what: Decides whether a value and unit may be used as a model quantity. For known fact types it needs a finite number and a unit of the right dimension. For unknown types it allows only non-numeric values.
sections.why: Stated in the code: unknown quantitative properties remain evidence and are never model quantities.
sections.watch_out: Booleans and very large integers are rejected, and numbers with unknown fact types are never used by the model.

summary: Holds the lookup tables that say which unit names are known, which dimension each fact type should have, and whether a value may be used as a model quantity.
purpose: Stops unit mistakes, such as a voltage given in metres, from reaching the model, and avoids guessing units.
why: Stated in the header: quantity dimensions are explicit, with no calendar or undocumented unit inference.
how: 1. Lists known unit names with their standard unit, dimension and exact conversion factor. 2. Maps fact types such as width, voltage, count, duration and angle to a dimension. 3. Provides a helper that normalizes text for comparison. 4. Provides a check that a value and unit are finite numbers with a unit of the right dimension; unknown fact types are never model quantities.
inputs: Unit names and fact type names as text, plus a value for the model check.
outputs: Lookup tables, a normalized text key, and a yes or no answer on whether a value may drive the model.
risks: Short names such as a, d and h are matched exactly, so a mislabeled unit would be converted wrongly. Booleans and very large integers are rejected. Any fact type not in the map cannot be a model quantity.
debug: If a value is never used in the model, first check its fact type is in the dimension map and its unit is in the unit table with the same dimension. If a conversion looks wrong, check the multiplier for that unit.
